Q: Apache mod_rewrite - how do I compare parts of QUERY_STRING and HTTP_REFERER A:

(Aside: I don't see why this is a newfangled "discussion" type question as opposed to a regular Q&A?!)

This essentially boils down to a regex question, as this can be resolved using a single regex that uses an internal backreference to assert that the foo parameter has the same value in the QUERY_STRING and the HTTP_REFERER. (Consequently this can be handled with a single RewriteCond directive.)

I'm assuming the foo URL parameter is allowed to occur anywhere in the QUERY_STRING and anywhere in the HTTP_REFERER. The value of the foo parameter is 1 or more 0-9, a-z characters. If there is a minimum length then this should also be stated to further restrict the regex.

For example, to send a 403 Forbidden response when the check fails:

# Block any request where the same "foo=<value>" param does not occur in both the requested query string and HTTP Referer string 
RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING}@%{HTTP_REFERER} !(?:^|&)(foo=[\da-z]+)(?:&[^@]*)?@[^\?]+.*?(?:\?|&)\1(?:&[^@]*)?$
RewriteRule ^ - [F]

Explanation:

  • %{QUERY_STRING}@%{HTTP_REFERER} - The TestString - The query string and HTTP Referer are concatenated with a @ separater. The @ is just an arbitrary character that cannot occur elsewhere in the query string or Referer string. This allows us to determine the end of the query string and start of the HTTP Referer in the CondPattern (regex). In its simplest valid form, this will be a string of the form:

    foo=1a2b3c@http://example.com/?foo=1a2b3c

  • (?:^|&)(foo=[\da-z]+) - Matches the foo URL parameter anywhere in the query string. The entire foo=<value> pair is captured, rather than just the <value>, which avoids having to repeat the parameter name (foo) in the 2nd part of the regex.

  • (?:&[^@]*)? - skips the remaining query string (if any).

  • @ - matches a literal @ - the separator between the QUERY_STRING and HTTP_REFERER in the RewriteCond TestString.

  • [^\?]+ - skips ahead (greedy) to the query string on the HTTP Referer.

  • .*? - skips (non-greedy) any unrelated URL params (at least allows for the param we are interested in to not be at the start of the Referer's query string).

  • (?:\?|&)\1 - Matches the same URL parameter we have just captured from the query string (ie. foo=<value>) in the HTTP Referer's query string (either at the start, ie. preceded by ?, or subsequent param preceded by &). The \1 is an internal backreference that holds the value of first capturing group in the regex (ie. foo=<value> if successful). So, if the requested query string contains foo=1a2b3c, then that is exactly what we are attempting to match in the HTTP Referer.

  • (?:&[^@]*)?$ - Matches the remainder of the HTTP Referer (if any). This cannot contain a literal @. This basically prevents a malicious request that contains a manipulated query string that repeats the foo=<value> URL param and injected @ character that could otherwise get around the HTTP Referer check.

  • Finally, the ! prefix on the CondPattern (not technically part of the regex) negates the entire regex/expression. So, the RewriteCond directive is successful when the regex fails.

You don't need the L flag when the F flag is used as it is implied.

Note that this will naturally block direct requests (URL typed into the browser) and anytime the full HTTP Referer is not passed (due to user settings or site referrer policy). I assume you are ensuring that any inbound links also have this query string in their URL - if that is a requirement. (Consequently this will also likely block search engine bots, that generally do not send a Referer.)
